title: Choose and book an English test (OET or IELTS)
description: Before anything else, decide between OET (Occupational English Test, healthcare-specific) and IELTS Academic, and book a sitting. Most dentists find OET's healthcare-context material more directly relevant to clinical scenarios, but IELTS is more widely available in some countries. Check the GDC's current accepted-test list and minimum score requirements before booking, as these are occasionally revised.

title: Prepare for and sit OET
description: Structured preparation for OET (typically Reading, Listening, Writing, Speaking modules in a healthcare context), followed by sitting the exam and awaiting results.

title: Prepare for and sit IELTS Academic
description: Structured preparation for IELTS Academic (Reading, Listening, Writing, Speaking), followed by sitting the exam and awaiting results.

title: Understand the GDC overseas registration route
description: Dentists who qualified outside the UK/EEA (and most who qualified in the EEA after the relevant cut-off) generally register with the GDC via the Overseas Registration Exam (ORE) route, administered in two parts. Review the GDC's current eligibility criteria for your qualifying country and degree before applying, since requirements vary and are periodically updated.

title: Prepare for ORE Part 1
description: ORE Part 1 is a written exam (multiple choice / EMQ style) covering core dental sciences and clinical knowledge. Most candidates use dedicated ORE prep courses or question banks alongside revision of UK-curriculum dental textbooks.

title: Sit ORE Part 1
description: Book and sit the ORE Part 1 written exam. Results determine eligibility to book ORE Part 2 (the clinical/practical assessment).

title: Re-prepare for an ORE Part 1 resit
description: If Part 1 was not passed, review the score breakdown to identify weak areas, allow a focused revision period, and rebook. There is typically a limit on the number of attempts — check current GDC guidance before resitting.

title: Prepare for ORE Part 2
description: ORE Part 2 is a practical/clinical assessment of manual and clinical skills, typically run over several days at a UK dental school test centre. Hands-on practice on phantom heads/models and familiarity with UK clinical protocols and materials is essential preparation.

title: Sit ORE Part 2
description: Book and sit the ORE Part 2 clinical assessment. Demand for test slots is high and booking windows can be limited — check availability and book early once eligible.

title: Apply for full GDC registration
description: Once exam/exemption requirements and English-language requirements are met, submit the formal application for full GDC registration, including identity, qualification, and fitness-to-practise documentation. Processing times vary, so apply as soon as you are eligible.

title: Build a UK-format dental CV and portfolio
description: UK dental CVs differ from many other countries' formats: typically reverse-chronological, 2 pages, with a focus on clinical procedures performed, CPD/courses, and references contactable by UK practices. Build this in parallel with exams/registration rather than waiting until the end.

title: Search and apply for UK dental positions
description: Search NHS and/or private practice vacancies (depending on preference), tailoring applications per role. Performer Number / NHS Pension setup is a separate administrative step once an NHS offer is in hand.

title: Prepare for UK dental practice interviews
description: UK dental interviews commonly include clinical scenario questions, communication/ethics questions, and sometimes a practical assessment. Prepare structured answers and, if relevant, research the practice's NHS/private mix in advance.

title: Understand UK visa sponsorship requirements
description: Most non-UK/Irish dentists need employer-sponsored work visa to take up a UK role (commonly the Skilled Worker visa route). Sponsorship requires the employer to hold a sponsor licence, and there are salary-threshold and eligibility rules that are updated periodically — verify current figures directly on GOV.UK before relying on them.

title: Apply for a Skilled Worker visa once sponsored
description: After accepting an offer from an employer holding a sponsor licence, you'll receive a Certificate of Sponsorship and can apply for the Skilled Worker visa. Processing times and documentary requirements should be checked on GOV.UK at the time of application, as they change.

title: Consider alternative dental-team routes while pursuing full registration
description: Some candidates work as a registered dental nurse, dental therapist, or dental hygienist (each has its own GDC registration route and scope of practice) while completing the dentist registration pathway, for UK clinical experience and income. These are genuine alternative or parallel career routes, not shortcuts to full dentist registration — check current GDC scope-of-practice and registration requirements for each role.
